claim: Interactions between top-down attention and bottom-up visceral inputs are assumed to produce conscious perceptions of interoceptive states.
source: Interactions between top-down attention and bottom-up visceral inputs are assumed to produce conscious perceptions of interoceptive states
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about interoceptive processing that draws from established scientific understanding in the field.

claim: Each process (top-down attention and bottom-up visceral inputs) has been independently associated with aberrant interoceptive symptomatology in psychiatric disorders.
source: while each process has been independently associated with aberrant interoceptive symptomatology in psychiatric disorders
evidence: This statement references prior research findings about the association between these processes and psychiatric symptoms.

claim: The neural substrates of the interface between top-down attention and bottom-up visceral inputs are unknown.
source: the neural substrates of this interface are unknown
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current scientific knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: The study included 46 individuals with anxiety, depression, and/or eating disorders (ADE) and 46 propensity-matched healthy comparisons (HC).
source: We conducted a preregistered functional neuroimaging study of 46 individuals with anxiety, depression, and/or eating disorders (ADE) and 46 propensity-matched healthy comparisons (HC)
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study design and sample composition.

claim: During an interoceptive attention task, top-down attention was voluntarily directed towards cardiorespiratory or visual signals.
source: During an interoceptive attention task, top-down attention was voluntarily directed towards cardiorespiratory or visual signals.
evidence: This describes the experimental manipulation in one of the tasks.

claim: Intravenous infusions of isoproterenol were administered in a double-blinded and placebo-controlled fashion during an interoceptive perturbation task.
source: during an interoceptive perturbation task, intravenous infusions of isoproterenol (a peripherally-acting beta-adrenergic receptor agonist) were administered in a double-blinded and placebo-controlled fashion
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the perturbation task.

claim: Isoproterenol is a peripherally-acting beta-adrenergic receptor agonist.
source: isoproterenol (a peripherally-acting beta-adrenergic receptor agonist)
evidence: This is a pharmacological characterization of the drug used in the study.

claim: Isoproterenol was used to drive bottom-up cardiorespiratory sensations.
source: intravenous infusions of isoproterenol (a peripherally-acting beta-adrenergic receptor agonist) were administered in a double-blinded and placebo-controlled fashion to drive bottom-up cardiorespiratory sensations
evidence: This describes the purpose and effect of the isoproterenol infusion.

claim: Neural activation converged upon the insular cortex across both tasks.
source: Across both tasks, neural activation converged upon the insular cortex
evidence: This is a primary finding from the neuroimaging analysis.

claim: Neural activation localized within the granular and ventral dysgranular subregions of the insula bilaterally.
source: Across both tasks, neural activation converged upon the insular cortex, localizing within the granular and ventral dysgranular subregions bilaterally.
evidence: This specifies the anatomical location of the convergent activation.

claim: The ADE group exhibited an asymmetric pattern of overlap in the left insula relative to HCs.
source: the ADE group exhibiting (relative to HCs) an asymmetric pattern of overlap in the left insula
evidence: This describes a group difference in the pattern of neural activation.

claim: The ADE group showed increased proportions of co-activated voxels within the left dysgranular insula.
source: the ADE group exhibiting (relative to HCs) an asymmetric pattern of overlap in the left insula, with increased or decreased proportions of co-activated voxels within the left or right dysgranular insula, respectively
evidence: This quantifies the hemispheric difference in the ADE group.

claim: The ADE group showed decreased proportions of co-activated voxels within the right dysgranular insula.
source: the ADE group exhibiting (relative to HCs) an asymmetric pattern of overlap in the left insula, with increased or decreased proportions of co-activated voxels within the left or right dysgranular insula, respectively
evidence: This quantifies the hemispheric difference in the ADE group.

claim: The ADE group showed less agranular anterior insula activation during periods of bodily uncertainty.
source: The ADE group also showed less agranular anterior insula activation during periods of bodily uncertainty (i.e. when anticipating possible isoproterenol-induced changes that never arrived).
evidence: This describes a group difference in activation during a specific task condition.

claim: Post-task changes in insula functional connectivity were associated with anxiety and depression severity.
source: Finally, post-task changes in insula functional connectivity were associated with anxiety and depression severity.
evidence: This describes a correlation between neural measures and clinical symptoms.

claim: The dysgranular mid-insula is a key cortical interface where attention and prediction meet real-time bodily inputs.
source: These findings confirm the dysgranular mid-insula as a key cortical interface where attention and prediction meet real-time bodily inputs, especially during heightened awareness of interoceptive states.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings based on the observed convergence of top-down and bottom-up processing.

claim: The dysgranular mid-insula is especially important during heightened awareness of interoceptive states.
source: These findings confirm the dysgranular mid-insula as a key cortical interface where attention and prediction meet real-time bodily inputs, especially during heightened awareness of interoceptive states.
evidence: This is an inference based on the task conditions that elicited the strongest activation.

claim: The dysgranular mid-insula may be a 'locus of disruption' for psychiatric disorders.
source: Furthermore, the dysgranular mid-insula may indeed be a 'locus of disruption' for psychiatric disorders.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observed group differences in activation patterns.

claim: Maintaining the body in a physiologically optimal state is a primary function of the mammalian nervous system.
source: Maintaining the body in a physiologically optimal state is a primary function of the mammalian nervous system.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: The neurovisceral architecture depends on the hierarchical central processing of peripheral internal body signals.
source: The neurovisceral architecture accomplishing such feats depends on the hierarchical central processing of peripheral internal body signals and operates hierarchically and across heterogenous time scales (Smith et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The neurovisceral architecture operates hierarchically and across heterogenous time scales.
source: The neurovisceral architecture accomplishing such feats depends on the hierarchical central processing of peripheral internal body signals and operates hierarchically and across heterogenous time scales (Smith et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Homeostasis involves automatically returning the internal state to a setpoint.
source: automatically returning the internal state to a setpoint (i.e. homeostasis) (Cannon, 1939)
evidence: This is a definition of homeostasis supported by a classic citation.

claim: Allostasis involves shifting the internal state away from a setpoint in anticipation of future deviations.
source: or shifting the internal state away from a setpoint in anticipation of future deviations (i.e. allostasis) (Sterling, 2012)
evidence: This is a definition of allostasis supported by a citation.

claim: Regulatory operations may depend on both unconscious and conscious monitoring of interoceptive states.
source: Importantly, these regulatory operations may depend on the unconscious as well as conscious monitoring of interoceptive states.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about interoceptive processing.

claim: Interoceptive sensations may dominate awareness during significant physiological disturbances.
source: Interoceptive sensations may even dominate awareness during significant physiological disturbances, motivating behaviors that restore bodily states to homeostatic equilibrium (Khalsa and Lapidus, 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Interoceptive sensations motivate behaviors that restore bodily states to homeostatic equilibrium.
source: Interoceptive sensations may even dominate awareness during significant physiological disturbances, motivating behaviors that restore bodily states to homeostatic equilibrium (Khalsa and Lapidus, 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Interoceptive sensations form the basis for emotional experience and numerous cognitive processes.
source: and forming the basis for emotional experience and numerous cognitive processes (Adolfi et al., 2017; Carvalho and Damasio, 2021; Critchley and Garfinkel, 2017; Uddin et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Dysfunctional interoception has been implicated in the pathophysiology of psychiatric disorders.
source: In turn, dysfunctional interoception has been implicated in the pathophysiology of psychiatric (Bonaz et al., 2021; Khalsa et al., 2018) and neurological disorders (Birba et al., 2022; Drane et al., 2020)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Dysfunctional interoception has been implicated in the pathophysiology of neurological disorders.
source: In turn, dysfunctional interoception has been implicated in the pathophysiology of psychiatric (Bonaz et al., 2021; Khalsa et al., 2018) and neurological disorders (Birba et al., 2022; Drane et al., 2020)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Conscious interoceptive perceptions must reflect the organism's current physiological state to a considerable extent.
source: Conscious interoceptive perceptions must, to a considerable extent, reflect the organism's current physiological state.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about the nature of interoceptive perception.

claim: Physiological state is hierarchically conveyed to the brain by cascades of peripheral interoceptive inputs.
source: This is hierarchically conveyed to the brain by cascades of peripheral interoceptive inputs, from vagal and spinal afferent nerves relaying signals transduced from interoceptors located throughout the major internal organ systems (e.g. cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urogenital), as well as via direct chemo humoral signaling (Berntson and Khalsa, 2021).
evidence: This describes the anatomical pathways of interoceptive signaling, supported by a citation.

claim: Vagal and spinal afferent nerves relay signals transduced from interoceptors located throughout major internal organ systems.
source: from vagal and spinal afferent nerves relaying signals transduced from interoceptors located throughout the major internal organ systems (e.g. cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urogenital)
evidence: This describes the anatomical pathways of interoceptive signaling.

claim: Interoceptive signals are conveyed via direct chemohumoral signaling.
source: as well as via direct chemo humoral signaling (Berntson and Khalsa, 2021)
evidence: This describes an additional pathway for interoceptive signaling, supported by a citation.

claim: Ascending interoceptive pathways converge via brainstem and thalamic nuclei onto the insular cortex.
source: Ascending interoceptive pathways converge via brainstem and thalamic nuclei onto the insular cortex, a structurally and functionally diverse region suggested to be the integrative hub for interoceptive awareness, emotional feelings, and overall body awareness (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2009)
evidence: This describes the neuroanatomical pathway of interoceptive signals, supported by citations.

claim: The insular cortex is a structurally and functionally diverse region.
source: Ascending interoceptive pathways converge via brainstem and thalamic nuclei onto the insular cortex, a structurally and functionally diverse region suggested to be the integrative hub for interoceptive awareness, emotional feelings, and overall body awareness (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2009)
evidence: This is a characterization of the insular cortex supported by citations.

claim: The insular cortex is suggested to be the integrative hub for interoceptive awareness, emotional feelings, and overall body awareness.
source: Ascending interoceptive pathways converge via brainstem and thalamic nuclei onto the insular cortex, a structurally and functionally diverse region suggested to be the integrative hub for interoceptive awareness, emotional feelings, and overall body awareness (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2009)
evidence: This is a theoretical claim about the function of the insular cortex, supported by citations.

claim: A principal role for the insular cortex in interoceptive awareness is supported by previous functional neuroimaging studies.
source: A principal role for the insular cortex in interoceptive awareness is supported by previous functional neuroimaging studies from our group, which have highlighted the insula as the primary region dynamically tracking pharmacological perturbations of the heart and lungs in both healthy individuals (Hassanpour et al., 2016; Hassanpour et al., 2018), and those with generalized anxiety disorder (Teed et al., 2022)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research from the authors' group.

claim: The insula is the primary region dynamically tracking pharmacological perturbations of the heart and lungs in healthy individuals.
source: which have highlighted the insula as the primary region dynamically tracking pharmacological perturbations of the heart and lungs in both healthy individuals (Hassanpour et al., 2016; Hassanpour et al., 2018)
evidence: This is a finding from prior research by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The insula is the primary region dynamically tracking pharmacological perturbations of the heart and lungs in those with generalized anxiety disorder.
source: which have highlighted the insula as the primary region dynamically tracking pharmacological perturbations of the heart and lungs in both healthy individuals (Hassanpour et al., 2016; Hassanpour et al., 2018), and those with generalized anxiety disorder (Teed et al., 2022)
evidence: This is a finding from prior research by the authors, supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple subregions of the insula are involved in bottom-up processing of afferently relayed cardiorespiratory signals, including the dysgranular mid and granular posterior sectors.
source: Our studies have identified multiple subregions of the insula in this 'bottom-up' processing of afferently relayed cardiorespiratory signals, including the dysgranular mid and granular posterior sectors
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' prior research.

claim: The identification of dysgranular mid and granular posterior insula subregions in bottom-up processing is in general agreement with existing theoretical and cytoarchitectonic arguments regarding their function.
source: Our studies have identified multiple subregions of the insula in this 'bottom-up' processing of afferently relayed cardiorespiratory signals, including the dysgranular mid and granular posterior sectors, in general agreement with existing theoretical (Barrett and Simmons, 2015; Fermin et al., 2022) and cytoarchitectonic (Evrard, 2019) arguments regarding their function.
evidence: This statement connects the authors' findings to existing theoretical frameworks, supported by citations.

claim: Cortical sensitivity to ascending signals is presumptively required for conscious detection of internal physiological shifts in humans.
source: While cortical sensitivity to ascending signals is presumptively required for conscious detection of internal physiological shifts in humans
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about the requirements for conscious interoception.

claim: Subjective perceptions are not simply veridical reflections of ascending inputs, faithfully transmitted and reproduced in a dormant sensory cortex.
source: accumulating evidence also suggests that subjective perceptions (in any sensory modality) are not simply veridical reflections of these ascending inputs, faithfully transmitted and reproduced in a dormant sensory cortex (Clark, 2013; Corbetta et al., 2008; Mechelli et al., 2004; Pace-Schott et al., 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Intrinsic top-down processes modulate the activity of sensory cortices, including the insula.
source: Instead, intrinsic 'top-down' processes also appear to modulate the activity of sensory cortices (including the insula), potentially altering the resulting percept in the process.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about top-down modulation of sensory processing.

claim: Internal models of the body that anticipate the sensory consequences of descending regulation can adjust the precision-weighting of prediction error signals in a context-specific manner.
source: For example, internal models of the body that anticipate the sensory consequences of descending regulation can adjust the precision-weighting of prediction error signals in a context-specific manner, increasing or decreasing the sensory processing of interoceptive inputs (Clark, 2016; Petzschner et al., 2021; Pezzulo et al., 2015; Seth and Friston, 2016).
evidence: This statement describes a predictive coding mechanism, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Focusing voluntary attention towards certain environmental signals alters their conscious experience and selectively enhances neural activity in the responsive area of cortex.
source: Extending beyond these model-based influences are goal-directed activities (also described previously as the 'attentional spotlight' effect Brefczynski and DeYoe, 1999), whereby focusing voluntary attention towards certain environmental signals not only alters their conscious experience but selectively enhances neural activity in the responsive area of cortex.
evidence: This statement describes the attentional spotlight effect, supported by a citation.

claim: Goal-directed shifts in attention towards endogenous visceral signals have consistently identified activation of the mid insular cortex in healthy individuals.
source: With respect to interoception, such goal-directed shifts in attention towards endogenous visceral signals have consistently identified activation of the mid insular cortex in healthy individuals (Avery et al., 2017; Simmons et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Abnormal mid insula activity has been associated with symptoms in those with eating disorders.
source: and revealed abnormal mid insula activity associated with symptoms in those with eating disorders (Kerr et al., 2016), depression (Avery et al., 2014; Burrows et al., 2022), and substance use disorders (Stewart et al., 2020)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Abnormal mid insula activity has been associated with symptoms in those with depression.
source: and revealed abnormal mid insula activity associated with symptoms in those with eating disorders (Kerr et al., 2016), depression (Avery et al., 2014; Burrows et al., 2022), and substance use disorders (Stewart et al., 2020)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Abnormal mid insula activity has been associated with symptoms in those with substance use disorders.
source: and revealed abnormal mid insula activity associated with symptoms in those with eating disorders (Kerr et al., 2016), depression (Avery et al., 2014; Burrows et al., 2022), and substance use disorders (Stewart et al., 2020)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Conscious perceptions of interoceptive signals are underpinned by reciprocal interactions between bottom-up, ascending interoceptive afferents and the coupled, top-down descending efferent systems that enact adaptive regulation and attentional control.
source: Conscious perceptions of interoceptive signals are thus underpinned by reciprocal interactions between bottom-up, ascending interoceptive afferents and the coupled, top-down descending efferent systems that enact adaptive regulation and attentional control (Berntson and Khalsa, 2021).
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about interoceptive processing, supported by a citation.

claim: The insula is uniquely positioned to serve as a cortical interface between top-down and bottom-up information streams for the processing of interoceptive signals.
source: Based on the available evidence, the insula is uniquely positioned to serve as a cortical interface between these two information streams for the processing of interoceptive signals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical and functional properties of the insula.

claim: The mammalian insula is highly interconnected with other cortical, subcortical, and brainstem areas.
source: The highly interconnected nature of the mammalian insula with other cortical (prefrontal Mufson and Mesulam, 1982, somatosensory Augustine, 1996, cingulate Mufson and Mesulam, 1982 cortices), subcortical (amygdala, thalamus Gehrlach et al., 2020), and brainstem (Gogolla, 2017) areas
evidence: This statement describes the anatomical connectivity of the insula, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The insula's connectivity facilitates the ability for salient bottom-up activity to recruit conscious attention mechanisms and/or give rise to perceptions and feelings that can adaptively drive behavior and promote homeostatic regulation.
source: The highly interconnected nature of the mammalian insula with other cortical (prefrontal Mufson and Mesulam, 1982, somatosensory Augustine, 1996, cingulate Mufson and Mesulam, 1982 cortices), subcortical (amygdala, thalamus Gehrlach et al., 2020), and brainstem (Gogolla, 2017) areas facilitates the ability for salient bottom-up activity to recruit conscious attention mechanisms and/or give rise to perceptions and feelings that can adaptively drive behavior and promote homeostatic regulation (Evrard, 2019).
evidence: This is a functional interpretation of the insula's connectivity, supported by a citation.

claim: Disrupted processing in the insula may be characteristic of individuals with certain psychiatric disorders.
source: Furthermore, disrupted processing in this region may be characteristic of individuals with certain psychiatric disorders.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of the insula in psychopathology.

claim: Abnormal activation of the left dorsal mid-insula differentiated healthy individuals from groups of individuals with anorexia nervosa, anxiety disorders, depression, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia.
source: In a previous human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) meta-analysis, abnormal activation of the left dorsal mid-insula differentiated healthy individuals from groups of individuals with anorexia nervosa, anxiety disorders, depression, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia, across tasks involving the bottom-up modulation of pain, dyspnea, or hunger or the top-down manipulation of interoceptive attention (Nord et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement summarizes findings from a prior meta-analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: The left dorsal mid-insula was inferred as a possible transdiagnostic and domain-general neuromarker of psychopathology.
source: This insular 'locus of disruption' was inferred as a possible transdiagnostic and domain-general neuro marker of psychopathology
evidence: This is an interpretation from a prior meta-analysis.

claim: The mid-insula is an important area for interoceptive dysfunction and a putative target for clinical intervention.
source: and the finding advanced the field by pointing toward the mid-insula as an important area for interoceptive dysfunction and a putative target for clinical intervention (Paulus and Khalsa, 2021)
evidence: This is a clinical implication drawn from prior research, supported by a citation.

claim: No study to date has directly investigated both interoceptive processing streams together in the same sample.
source: Despite the theoretical and empirical convergence related to bottom-up and top-down processing in the insula, no study to date has directly investigated both interoceptive processing streams together in the same sample.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claim: The study conducted a pre-registered conjunction analysis of two established neuroimaging tasks preferentially manipulating the assessment of top-down and bottom-up interoception.
source: Here, we conducted a pre-registered conjunction analysis of two established neuroimaging tasks preferentially manipulating the assessment of top-down and bottom-up interoception (Adamic et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the study design and methodology.

claim: Broad regions of the dysgranular mid insula would be co-activated when engaging top-down interoceptive attention under physiological resting conditions and during bottom-up perturbation of peripheral interoceptive signals via isoproterenol.
source: Our hypotheses, based on a voxelwise whole-brain approach, were threefold: (1) broad regions of the dysgranular mid insula would be co-activated when (a) engaging top-down interoceptive attention under physiological resting conditions and (b) during bottom-up perturbation of peripheral interoceptive signals via the adrenergic drug isoproterenol
evidence: This is a pre-registered hypothesis of the study.

claim: The agranular anterior insula would be preferentially selective to manipulations of interoceptive uncertainty, such as those occurring during saline infusions.
source: (2) the agranular anterior insula would be preferentially selective to manipulations of interoceptive uncertainty, such as those occurring during saline infusions
evidence: This is a pre-registered hypothesis of the study.

claim: Relative to healthy individuals, interoceptive processing in the insula would show lateralized differences across a transdiagnostic group of individuals with anxiety, depression, and/or eating disorders.
source: (3) relative to healthy individuals, interoceptive processing in the insula would show lateralized differences across a transdiagnostic group of individuals with anxiety, depression, and/or eating disorders
evidence: This is a pre-registered hypothesis of the study.

claim: Of the 127 total participants included in this study, 57 ADE individuals and 46 HC individuals fulfilled the criteria for high-quality brain imaging data with both tasks.
source: Of the 127 total participants included in this study, 57 ADE individuals and 46 HC individuals fulfilled the criteria for high-quality brain imaging data with both tasks.
evidence: This describes the sample after quality control procedures.

claim: Most of the participants were female, in line with the predominant female prevalence of these disorders.
source: In line with the predominant female prevalence of these disorders, most of the participants were female.
evidence: This describes the sex distribution of the sample and relates it to disorder prevalence.

claim: Propensity matching on age, self-reported sex, and body mass index resulted in 46 individuals per group.
source: To obtain equal-sized groups for group-level comparison, propensity matching on age, self-reported sex, and body mass index resulted in 46 individuals per group (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the statistical matching procedure used to create comparable groups.

claim: After propensity matching, the two groups were not significantly different regarding age, body mass index, and sex.
source: After propensity matching, the two groups were not significantly different regarding age, body mass index, and sex
evidence: This confirms the success of the propensity matching procedure.

claim: After propensity matching, the groups differed significantly on trait measures of anxiety (STAI), anxiety sensitivity (ASI, Total and subscales), depression (PHQ-9), and eating disorders (SCOFF).
source: but they differed significantly on trait measures of anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory; STAI), anxiety sensitivity (Anxiety Sensitivity Index; ASI, Total and subscales), depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9; PHQ-9) (Kroenke et al., 2001), and eating disorders (Sick, Control, One, Fat, Food questionnaire; SCOFF) (Kutz et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the clinical differences between groups after matching.

claim: All participants in the ADE group exhibited some form of psychiatric comorbidity.
source: All participants in the ADE group exhibited some form of psychiatric comorbidity.
evidence: This describes the clinical characteristics of the ADE group.

claim: 67% of the ADE group had a diagnosis of GAD (current or lifetime).
source: Across the group, 67% had a diagnosis of GAD (current or lifetime)
evidence: This quantifies the prevalence of GAD in the ADE group.

claim: 72% of the ADE group had major depression (current or remitted).
source: 72% of major depression (current or remitted)
evidence: This quantifies the prevalence of major depression in the ADE group.

claim: 35% of the ADE group had anorexia nervosa (current or lifetime).
source: and 35% of anorexia nervosa (current or lifetime)
evidence: This quantifies the prevalence of anorexia nervosa in the ADE group.

claim: Most ADE participants reported taking psychiatric medication.
source: Most ADE participants reported taking psychiatric medication (see Table 1 for details).
evidence: This describes medication use in the ADE group.

claim: Bilateral patches of the ventral mid-insular cortex were commonly activated during the ISO and VIA tasks.
source: Bilateral patches of the ventral mid-insular cortex were commonly activated during the ISO and VIA tasks (Figure 2) (Table 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the convergence analysis, supported by figures and tables.

claim: Convergent clusters were localized primarily to the dysgranular insula bilaterally.
source: Quantification of the spatial extent of this convergence in the pre-defined probabilistic agranular, dysgranular, and granular subregions revealed that these convergent clusters were localized primarily to the dysgranular insula bilaterally (Figure 3A)
evidence: This quantifies the anatomical location of the convergent activation.

claim: There was a hemispheric asymmetry in convergence across groups.
source: but with a hemispheric asymmetry across groups
evidence: This describes a key group difference in the pattern of convergence.

claim: The spatial similarity of convergently activated voxels between the groups was lower for the left dysgranular insula (Dice coefficient of 0.58) than for the right (Dice coefficient of 0.78).
source: Correspondingly, the spatial similarity of these convergently activated voxels between the groups was lower for the left dysgranular insula (Dice coefficient of 0.58) than for the right (Dice coefficient of 0.78) (Figure 2).
evidence: This quantifies the spatial similarity of activation patterns between groups.

claim: There was a lower amount of overlap between the two tasks in the left dysgranular insula for both groups.
source: In addition to these group hemispheric differences in spatial extent, there was a lower amount of overlap between the two tasks in the left dysgranular insula for both groups (left hemisphere overlap coefficients: 0.42 and 0.63 for HC and ADE, respectively; right hemisphere overlap coefficients: 0.83 and 0.78, for HC and ADE, respectively).
evidence: This quantifies the degree of task overlap within each hemisphere and group.

claim: The magnitude of activation within convergent dysgranular subregions during the Peak of perturbation or Heart and Lung attention was not different between groups.
source: Despite these group differences in the spatial extent and spatial similarity of convergence, the magnitude of activation within convergent dysgranular subregions during the Peak of perturbation (ISO 2.0 mcg dose) or Heart and Lung attention (VIA task) was not different between groups (F1,90=0.64 and 0.05, p=0.43 and 0.82 for main effect of group in ISO and VIA tasks, respectively).
evidence: This is a statistical finding showing no group difference in activation magnitude.

claim: During both ISO and VIA task conditions, activation was greater within the right hemisphere than the left.
source: However, during both of these task conditions, activation was greater within the right hemisphere than the left (F1,90=6.13 and 5.10, p=0.015 and 0.027 for main effect of hemisphere during ISO and VIA tasks, respectively; t90=–2.48 and –2.25, p=0.02 and 0.03 for post-hoc contrasts between the left versus right hemisphere when collapsed across groups) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a statistical finding showing a hemispheric difference in activation magnitude.

claim: The hemispheric effect on activation magnitude was specific to interoceptive processing, as no similar hemispheric difference was seen during the exteroceptive condition of the VIA task.
source: This hemispheric effect on activation magnitude was specific to interoceptive processing, as no similar hemispheric difference was seen during the exteroceptive condition of the VIA task (F1,90=0.68, p=0.41).
evidence: This demonstrates the specificity of the hemispheric effect to interoceptive processing.

claim: The magnitude of activation within the right dysgranular convergent region during the peak of cardiorespiratory perturbation was associated with the intensity of real-time cardiorespiratory sensations.
source: Furthermore, the magnitude of activation within the right (but not the left) dysgranular convergent region during the peak of cardiorespiratory perturbation was associated with the intensity of real-time cardiorespiratory sensations (i.e. mean dial rating) during this period when examined across the entire sample (Pearson's r=0.12 and 0.21, p=0.25 and 0.046 for the left and right hemispheres, respectively; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a correlational finding linking neural activation to subjective perception.

claim: PSC in either convergent hemisphere during perturbation was not associated with objective measures of physiological arousal (mean change in heart rate).
source: Conversely, PSC in either convergent hemisphere during perturbation was not associated with objective measures of physiological arousal (i.e. mean change in heart rate, Pearson's r=0.11 and 0.09, p=0.31 and 0.40 for left and right hemispheres, respectively)
evidence: This is a null finding showing no correlation between neural activation and heart rate.

claim: PSC in convergent regions during perturbation was not associated with post-scan ratings of cardiac intensity.
source: post-scan ratings of cardiac intensity (Pearson's r=0.16 and 0.20, p=0.15 and 0.06)
evidence: This is a null finding showing no significant correlation.

claim: PSC in convergent regions during perturbation was not associated with post-scan ratings of respiratory intensity.
source: post-scan ratings of respiratory intensity (Pearson's r=0.12 and 0.06, p=0.26 and 0.58 for left and right hemispheres, respectively)
evidence: This is a null finding showing no correlation.

claim: PSC in convergent regions during perturbation was not associated with post-scan ratings of state anxiety.
source: post-scan ratings of state anxiety (Pearson's r=0.14 and 0.08, p=0.20 and 0.49 for left and right hemispheres, respectively)
evidence: This is a null finding showing no correlation.

claim: PSC in convergent regions during perturbation was not associated with trait measures of anxiety sensitivity (ASI-Total).
source: or trait measures of anxiety sensitivity (i.e. ASI-Total, Pearson's r=0.12 and 0.16, p=0.25 and 0.13 for left and right hemispheres, respectively)
evidence: This is a null finding showing no correlation.

claim: Pre- to post-task resting state functional connectivity of the convergent regions showed a pattern of differential change in the ADE compared to HC group.
source: Finally, pre- to post-task resting state functional connectivity of the convergent regions showed a pattern of differential change in the ADE compared to HC group
evidence: This describes a group difference in connectivity changes.

claim: Functional connectivity between the right dysgranular convergent cluster and left middle frontal gyrus increased in the ADE group only, while the HC group saw no differences.
source: functional connectivity between the right dysgranular convergent cluster and left middle frontal gyrus increased in the ADE group only, while the HC group saw no differences (p<0.05, corrected; Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding showing a group-specific connectivity change.

claim: The magnitude of functional connectivity change between the right dysgranular insula and left middle frontal gyrus was associated with trait anxiety (OASIS and GAD7).
source: When looking at this insular-IFG connection across the entire sample, the magnitude of functional connectivity change between these two areas was associated with trait anxiety (Pearson's r=0.43 and 0.36 for OASIS and GAD7, respectively, p<0.001)
evidence: This is a correlational finding linking connectivity changes to anxiety symptoms.

claim: The magnitude of functional connectivity change between the right dysgranular insula and left middle frontal gyrus was associated with trait depression (PHQ-9).

claim: The Anticipation period of the ISO task engaged large swaths of the bilateral agranular insular cortex that were not activated at any point during the VIA task.

claim: The spatial patterns of agranular activation during the Anticipation period were similar between groups (Dice coefficient = 0.86 in the left and 0.87 in the right).

claim: The signal intensity in the agranular insula increased from the Anticipation period to the Saline Peak period.
